```{r}
fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL) {
  df <- dplyr::mutate(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of("Year"), as.integer))
  right <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  flextable::flextable(df) |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::align(j = setdiff(names(df), right), align = "left", part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(j = right, align = "right", part = "body") |>
    flextable::colformat_int(big.mark = "") |>
    flextable::padding(padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1, part = "all") |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}
```

```{r}
# FAOSTAT Emissions from Fires (domain GI), FAO, Rome
# https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/GI
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv") &&
    nzchar(Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_USER")) && nzchar(Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_PASSWORD"))) {
  login <- httr2::request("https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/auth/login") |>
    httr2::req_body_form(username = Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_USER"),
                         password = Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_PASSWORD")) |>
    httr2::req_perform() |>
    httr2::resp_body_json()
  httr2::request("https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/en/data/GI") |>
    httr2::req_url_query(area = "33", area_cs = "FAO", output_type = "csv") |>
    httr2::req_auth_bearer_token(login$AuthenticationResult$AccessToken) |>
    httr2::req_perform(path = "02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv")
}

fires <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::select(item = Item, element = Element, year = Year, source = Source,
                value = Value, unit = Unit, flag = Flag)

forest_co2 <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", element == "Emissions (CO2)", source == "FAO TIER 1") |>
  dplyr::select(year, co2 = value)

forest <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", source == "FAO TIER 1",
                element %in% c("Burned Area", "Emissions (CO2)", "Emissions (CH4)"), year >= 2001) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::rename(Year = year, `Burned area (ha)` = `Burned Area`,
                `CO2 (kt)` = `Emissions (CO2)`, `CH4 (kt)` = `Emissions (CH4)`)

gap <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Other forest", element == "Emissions (CO2)") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = source, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(`FAO TIER 1`), !is.na(UNFCCC)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year, `FAO Tier 1 (kt)` = `FAO TIER 1`, `UNFCCC (kt)` = UNFCCC,
                   Ratio = round(`FAO TIER 1` / UNFCCC, 1))

# Tables 2.4 and 2.5 of the 2006 IPCC Guidelines, Volume 4, Chapter 2, pages 2.45 to 2.47, the tables the FAOSTAT methodological note cites
# http://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/index.html
table_2_4 <- tibble::tribble(~fuel, ~se, ~`Table 2.4 row`,
  41.0, 36.5, "All boreal forest", 50.4, 53.7, "All other temperate forests", 3.3, NA, "Savanna woodland, mid or late dry season burns",
  4.1, 3.1, "Grassland, mid or late dry season burns", 14.3, 9.0, "All shrublands", 26.7, 4.2, "Shrubland (general)")
table_2_5 <- tibble::tribble(~ef_row, ~co2, ~co2_sd, ~ch4, ~ch4_sd, ~n2o, ~n2o_sd,
  "Savanna and grassland", 1613, 95, 2.3, 0.9, 0.21, 0.10, "Extra tropical forest", 1569, 131, 4.7, 1.9, 0.26, 0.07)
used <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, item %in% c("Other forest", "Woody savanna", "Savanna", "Grassland", "Open shrubland", "Closed shrubland")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(element = dplyr::case_match(element, "Burned Area" ~ "ha", "Emissions (CO2)" ~ "co2", "Emissions (CH4)" ~ "ch4", "Emissions (N2O)" ~ "n2o", .default = "dm")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(item, year), names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(ha > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fuel = dm / ha, dplyr::across(c(co2, ch4, n2o), \(x) x * 1e6 / dm))
coefficients <- used |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = item, years = dplyr::n(), ha = sum(ha) / 24, fuel_min = min(fuel), fuel_max = max(fuel),
                   co2 = mean(co2), ch4 = mean(ch4), n2o = mean(n2o)) |>
  dplyr::filter(years == 24) |>
  dplyr::arrange(item != "Other forest", -ha) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Item = item,
    `Burned area (ha a year)` = format(round(ha), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
    `Fuel (t/ha)` = dplyr::if_else(round(fuel_min, 1) == round(fuel_max, 1), sprintf("%.1f", fuel_min), sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", fuel_min, fuel_max)),
    `Table 2.4 row` = dplyr::coalesce(table_2_4$`Table 2.4 row`[match(round(fuel_min, 1), table_2_4$fuel)], "Between all boreal forest and all other temperate forests"),
    `CH4 (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.1f", ch4), `N2O (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.2f", n2o),
    `CO2 (g/kg)` = dplyr::if_else(is.na(co2), "", format(round(co2), big.mark = ","))) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(Item = "Table 2.5, extra tropical forest", `Burned area (ha a year)` = "", `Fuel (t/ha)` = "", `Table 2.4 row` = "",
    `CH4 (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.1f", table_2_5$ch4[2]), `N2O (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.2f", table_2_5$n2o[2]), `CO2 (g/kg)` = format(table_2_5$co2[2], big.mark = ",")))
savanna_share <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, element == "Burned Area", item %in% c("Forest fires", "Savanna fires")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = item, values_from = value) |>

burned <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/nfdb/area-burned-by-province.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

trees_uncertainty <- function(ci_half_width) 0.524417 / 1.645006 * ci_half_width

buffer_table <- c(none = 0.25, `1` = 0.20, `2` = 0.15, `3` = 0.20,
                  `1,2` = 0.10, `1,3` = 0.15, `2,3` = 0.10, `1,2,3` = 0.05)

trees_buffer <- function(mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  buffer_table[[mitigating]] + if (after_reversal) 0.05 else 0
}

kept <- function(ci_half_width, mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  1 - trees_uncertainty(ci_half_width) - trees_buffer(mitigating, after_reversal)
}

break_even <- function(...) (1 - trees_buffer(...)) / (0.524417 / 1.645006)

crediting_level <- function(x, years) sum(x[years]) / 5

accounts <- national |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2012) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reference = year <= 2016)

level_split  <- sum(accounts$human[accounts$reference]) / 5
level_whole  <- sum(accounts$net[accounts$reference]) / 5

credits <- accounts |>

                   `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = human,

                   `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_whole - net, 1))

split_pos <- credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
whole_pos <- credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
worst <- which.min(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

bc_level_whole <- sum(bc_accounts$net[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5

bc_credits <- bc_accounts |>

bc_split_pos <- bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_whole_pos <- bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0

classify <- function(n) {
  base <- forest_co2[forest_co2$year < min(forest_co2$year) + n, ]
  thr <- mean(base$co2) + 2 * stats::sd(base$co2)
  data.frame(`Baseline (years)` = n,
             Period = if (nrow(base) < n) NA_character_ else
               paste(min(base$year), max(base$year), sep = "-"),
             `Threshold (kt)` = if (nrow(base) < n) NA_real_ else round(thr),
             `Years classified natural` = if (nrow(base) < n) "baseline longer than the series" else
               paste(forest_co2$year[forest_co2$co2 > thr], collapse = ", "),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
baselines <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(13, 20, 30), classify))

# The threshold rule on Canada's two lines: the natural disturbance line is left out only in a year whose
# forest fire emissions exceed the mean of the 13-year baseline, the length Australia's inventory uses, by two standard deviations
years13 <- forest_co2$year[forest_co2$year < min(forest_co2$year) + 13]
first13 <- forest_co2$co2[forest_co2$year %in% years13]
natural_years <- forest_co2$year[forest_co2$co2 > mean(first13) + 2 * stats::sd(first13)]
accounts <- dplyr::mutate(accounts, rule = dplyr::if_else(year %in% natural_years, human, net))
level_rule <- sum(accounts$rule[accounts$reference]) / 5
credits <- credits |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Threshold rule emissions (Mt)` = accounts$rule[!accounts$reference],
                `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(level_rule - `Threshold rule emissions (Mt)`, 1))
rule_pos <- credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
rule_out <- credits$Year %in% natural_years
rule_worst <- which.min(credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]])

# The threshold rule's second step for British Columbia: a nationally natural year counts as natural in the province only
# when the province's burned area exceeds its own mean over the same 13 years by one standard deviation
bc_burned <- dplyr::filter(burned, province == "BC")
bc_base <- bc_burned$hectares[bc_burned$year %in% years13]
bc_natural_years <- intersect(natural_years, bc_burned$year[bc_burned$hectares > mean(bc_base) + stats::sd(bc_base)])
bc_accounts <- dplyr::mutate(bc_accounts, rule = dplyr::if_else(year %in% bc_natural_years, human, net))
bc_level_rule <- sum(bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5
bc_credits <- bc_credits |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Threshold rule emissions (Mt)` = round(bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$year >= 2017], 1),
                `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_rule - bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$year >= 2017], 1))
bc_rule_pos <- bc_credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_rule_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]])
bc_threshold_ha <- mean(bc_base) + stats::sd(bc_base)
bc_ha <- \(y) bc_burned$hectares[bc_burned$year == y]

ci <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.50, 2.00)
deductions <- data.frame(
  `Uncertainty, 90% interval half width (%)` = ci * 100,
  `Uncertainty deduction (%)` = round(100 * trees_uncertainty(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 25% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 5% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, "1,2,3"), 1),
  `Kept, 30% buffer after a reversal (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, after_reversal = TRUE), 1),
  check.names = FALSE)

set.seed(42)
sd_mt <- 16.6 * (44 / 12) / 1.96

simulate_reductions <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) +
                             stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  level - (emissions + stats::rnorm(n, 0, sd_mt))
}

monte_carlo <- function(reference, series) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(series)), function(k) {
    draws <- simulate_reductions(reference, series$emissions[k])
    half <- (stats::quantile(draws, 0.95) - stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)) / 2
    data.frame(Year = series$year[k], mean = mean(draws), sd = stats::sd(draws), q05 = unname(stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)),
               q95 = unname(stats::quantile(draws, 0.95)), half = half, ci = half / abs(mean(draws)))
  }))
}

reference_split <- accounts$human[accounts$reference]
reference_whole <- accounts$net[accounts$reference]

mc_split <- monte_carlo(reference_split,
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))
mc_whole <- monte_carlo(reference_whole,
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))
mc_rule <- monte_carlo(accounts$rule[accounts$reference],
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]]))

blank_if_negative <- function(value, mean_reduction) ifelse(mean_reduction > 0, value, NA)

uncertainty <- data.frame(
  Year = mc_split$Year,
  `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_split$mean, 1),
  `Disaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_split$ci), mc_split$mean),
  `Disaggregated deduction (%)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * trees_uncertainty(mc_split$ci), 1), mc_split$mean),
  `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_whole$mean, 1),
  `Undisaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_whole$ci), mc_whole$mean),
  `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_rule$mean, 1),
  `Threshold rule interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_rule$ci), mc_rule$mean),
  `Threshold rule deduction (%)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * trees_uncertainty(mc_rule$ci), 1), mc_rule$mean),
  check.names = FALSE)

over <- uncertainty[["Disaggregated deduction (%)"]] > 100

# Display tables in the statistical terms of the draws, one row per year and account
account_levels <- c("Disaggregated", "Undisaggregated", "Threshold")
credits_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(Year = credits$Year, Account = "Disaggregated", E = credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]], CL = level_split),
  tibble::tibble(Year = credits$Year, Account = "Undisaggregated", E = credits[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]], CL = level_whole),
  tibble::tibble(Year = credits$Year, Account = "Threshold", E = credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]], CL = level_rule)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Year, factor(Account, account_levels)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(Year), Account, `Net emissions (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", E), `Crediting level (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL),
                   `Emission reduction (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL - E))
bc_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(Year = bc_credits$Year, Account = "Disaggregated", E = bc_credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]], CL = bc_level_split),
  tibble::tibble(Year = bc_credits$Year, Account = "Undisaggregated", E = bc_credits[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]], CL = bc_level_whole),
  tibble::tibble(Year = bc_credits$Year, Account = "Threshold", E = bc_credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]], CL = bc_level_rule)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Year, factor(Account, account_levels)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(bc_credits, Year, share = `Burned area share (%)`), by = "Year") |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(Year), Account, `Burned area share (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", share), `Net emissions (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", E),
                   `Crediting level (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL), `Emission reduction (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL - E))
uncertainty_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::mutate(mc_split, Account = "Disaggregated"), dplyr::mutate(mc_whole, Account = "Undisaggregated"),
                                      dplyr::mutate(mc_rule, Account = "Threshold")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Year, factor(Account, account_levels)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(Year), Account, `Mean reduction (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", mean), `Standard deviation (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", sd),
                   `5th percentile (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.0f", q05), `95th percentile (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.0f", q95),
                   `Relative half width (%)` = ifelse(mean > 0, sprintf("%.0f", 100 * ci), ""),
                   `Adjustment factor (%)` = ifelse(mean > 0, sprintf("%.1f", 100 * trees_uncertainty(ci)), ""))
banked <- ifelse(mc_split$mean > 0, 100 * purrr::map2_dbl(mc_split$ci, mc_split$Year > min(credits$Year[!split_pos]), \(ci, after) kept(ci, after_reversal = after)), NA)

msd <- \(x) sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f Mt CO~2~e a year (95 per cent confidence interval %.1f to %.1f)",
                    mean(x), stats::sd(x), stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[1], stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[2])
province <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "BC")

# Share of the annual error common to the reference years and the crediting year. A shared error cancels in
# the difference, the ground on which ART TREES excludes model error. The draws above share none. Under the
# normal model a shared share rho leaves the mean reduction and scales its half width by sqrt(1 - rho).
after <- credits$Year > min(credits$Year[!split_pos])
shared <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99), function(rho) {
  ci <- mc_split$ci * sqrt(1 - rho)
  data.frame(`Shared share` = rho,
             `Interval, lowest (%)` = round(100 * min(ci[split_pos])),
             `Interval, highest (%)` = round(100 * max(ci[split_pos])),
             `Years keeping a credit` = sum(purrr::map2_dbl(ci, after, \(h, a) kept(h, after_reversal = a))[split_pos] > 0),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
sh <- function(share, column) shared[[column]][shared[["Shared share"]] == share]
# The shared share at which every positive year keeps a credit, solved from the same scaling
rho_needed <- max(1 - (purrr::map_dbl(after[split_pos], \(a) break_even(after_reversal = a)) / mc_split$ci[split_pos])^2)

# Deduction the standard allows at the end of a crediting period, on the summed reference emissions minus the
# summed crediting period emissions, with the same independent draws
simulate_period <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  total <- length(emissions) * level -
    rowSums(matrix(rep(emissions, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(emissions), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  half <- unname((stats::quantile(total, 0.95) - stats::quantile(total, 0.05)) / 2)
  c(total = mean(total), half = half, ci = half / abs(mean(total)))
}
period_split <- simulate_period(reference_split, credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]])
period_rule <- simulate_period(accounts$rule[accounts$reference], credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]])
period_deduction <- period_split[["total"]] * trees_uncertainty(period_split[["ci"]])
yearly_deduction <- sum(mc_split$mean[split_pos] * trees_uncertainty(mc_split$ci[split_pos]))

# Approach 1 of the uncertainty chapter on the Tier 1 forest fire estimate: the relative uncertainty of a product
# is the square root of the sum of the squared relative uncertainties, each half a 95 per cent interval
u_term <- function(sd, mean) 1.96 * sd / mean
u_fuel <- u_term(table_2_4$se[1:2], table_2_4$fuel[1:2])
u_ef <- u_term(table_2_5$co2_sd[1], table_2_5$co2[1])
u_forest <- sqrt(u_fuel^2 + u_ef^2)
co2_2023 <- forest[["CO2 (kt)"]][forest$Year == 2023] / 1000
burn_2023 <- used[used$item == "Other forest" & used$year == 2023, ]
# 100 year global warming potentials of Canada's 2026 National Inventory Report, Table 1-1, 28 for CH4 and 265 for N2O
co2e_forest_row <- burn_2023$fuel * burn_2023$ha *
  ((table_2_5$ch4[2] - table_2_5$ch4[1]) * 28 + (table_2_5$n2o[2] - table_2_5$n2o[1]) * 265) / 1e9
```

```{r}
cover_of <- function(code) dplyr::case_when(code %in% 1:5 ~ cover_labels[1], code %in% 6:7 ~ cover_labels[2], code == 8 ~ cover_labels[3],
                                            code == 9 ~ cover_labels[4], code == 10 ~ cover_labels[5], code == 11 ~ cover_labels[6], .default = cover_labels[7])

# Every fire of 2001 to 2024 placed in its ecological zone, soil class, land cover class and province, with its cause, fire type and month
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/fires-by-stratum.csv") || !file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/large-fires.gpkg")) {
  points <- sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath("02.inputs/nfdb/raw/NFDB_point_shp.zip"), "/NFDB_point_20260811.shp"),
                        query = 'SELECT YEAR, MONTH, SIZE_HA, CAUSE, FIRE_TYPE, PRESCRIBED FROM "NFDB_point_20260811" WHERE YEAR >= 2001 AND YEAR <= 2024',
                        quiet = TRUE) |>
    sf::st_transform(3978) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cause = dplyr::case_when(CAUSE == "N" ~ "Natural", CAUSE == "H" ~ "Human", .default = "Unknown"),
                  type = dplyr::case_when(FIRE_TYPE == "Crown" ~ "Crown", FIRE_TYPE == "Surface" ~ "Surface", FIRE_TYPE == "Ground" ~ "Ground",
                                          FIRE_TYPE %in% c("Prescribed Burn", "PB") | PRESCRIBED == "PB" ~ "Prescribed", .default = "Unspecified"),
                  season = dplyr::case_when(MONTH %in% 4:5 ~ "April to May", MONTH == 6 ~ "June", MONTH == 7 ~ "July",
                                            MONTH %in% 8:10 ~ "August to October", .default = "Other months")) |>
    sf::st_join(gez[, "gez_abbrev"], join = sf::st_intersects, left = FALSE)
  wgs <- terra::vect(sf::st_transform(points, 4326))
  points$soil <- c("Unclassified", soil_labels)[dplyr::coalesce(terra::extract(soil, wgs)[, 2], 0) + 1]
  points$cover <- cover_of(terra::extract(land_cover, wgs)[, 2])
  points$bc <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(points, bc)) > 0
  sf::st_write(points[points$SIZE_HA >= 1000, c("YEAR", "SIZE_HA", "cause")], "02.inputs/ipcc/raw/large-fires.gpkg", quiet = TRUE, delete_dsn = TRUE)
  points |>
    sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
    dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(SIZE_HA), fires = dplyr::n(), .by = c(YEAR, gez_abbrev, soil, cover, cause, type, season, bc)) |>
    dplyr::rename(year = YEAR) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/ipcc/fires-by-stratum.csv")
}

# Equation 2.27 by stratum, each fire at the Table 2.4 row of its zone, fire type and month, and Equation 2.8 of the Wetlands Supplement added on organic soil
boreal_zones <- c("Ba", "Bb", "BM"); temperate_zones <- c("TeDc", "TeDo", "TeM"); grassland_zones <- c("TeBSk", "TeBWk")
row_of <- function(zone, type, season) dplyr::case_when(
  zone %in% boreal_zones & type == "Crown" ~ "Boreal forest, Crown fire",
  zone %in% boreal_zones & type == "Surface" ~ "Boreal forest, Surface fire",
  zone %in% boreal_zones ~ "Boreal forest, Wildfire (general)",
  zone %in% temperate_zones ~ "Other temperate forests, Wildfire",
  zone %in% grassland_zones & season %in% c("April to May", "June") ~ "Savanna grasslands and pastures, All savanna grasslands (early dry season burns)",
  zone %in% grassland_zones ~ "Savanna grasslands and pastures, Grassland (mid or late dry season burns)",
  zone == "P" ~ "Other vegetation types, Tundra")

  dplyr::inner_join(rows_2_4[, c("row", "mb_cf", "ef_row")], by = "row") |>

strata_2023 <- dplyr::filter(tier1_strata, year == 2023)
bc_2023_strata <- dplyr::filter(strata_2023, bc)
blocks <- c(cause = "Ignition", type = "Fire type", season = "Month", soil_group = "Soil class", cover = "Land cover")
summarise_strata <- function(d) {
  rows <- lapply(names(blocks), function(v) d |>
    dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), co2e = sum(co2e_mt), peat = sum(peat_co2e_mt), .by = dplyr::all_of(v)) |>
    dplyr::rename(class = dplyr::all_of(v)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(block = blocks[[v]]) |>
    dplyr::arrange(-ha))
  dplyr::bind_rows(rows, tibble::tibble(block = "All fires", class = "", ha = sum(d$ha), co2e = sum(d$co2e_mt), peat = sum(d$peat_co2e_mt)))
}
strata_table <- summarise_strata(strata_2023) |>
  dplyr::left_join(summarise_strata(bc_2023_strata), by = c("block", "class"), suffix = c("", "_bc")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(ha_bc, co2e_bc, peat_bc), \(x) dplyr::coalesce(x, 0))) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Stratum = dplyr::if_else(duplicated(block), "", block), Class = class,
                   `Canada burned (kha)` = sprintf("%.0f", ha / 1e3), `Canada vegetation CO2e (Mt)` = sprintf("%.1f", co2e),
                   `Canada organic soil CO2e (Mt)` = sprintf("%.1f", peat), `BC burned (kha)` = sprintf("%.0f", ha_bc / 1e3),
                   `BC vegetation CO2e (Mt)` = sprintf("%.1f", co2e_bc), `BC organic soil CO2e (Mt)` = sprintf("%.1f", peat_bc))
share <- function(d, var, levels) 100 * sum(d$ha[d[[var]] %in% levels]) / sum(d$ha)
natural_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "cause", "Natural"); human_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "cause", "Human")
natural_share_all <- share(tier1_strata, "cause", "Natural"); bc_natural_share_2023 <- share(bc_2023_strata, "cause", "Natural")
typed_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "type", c("Crown", "Surface", "Ground"))
organic_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "soil_group", "Organic"); bc_organic_share_2023 <- share(bc_2023_strata, "soil_group", "Organic")
forest_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "cover", cover_labels[1]); savanna_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "cover", cover_labels[3:4])
spring_share_2023 <- share(strata_2023, "season", "April to May")
veg_2023 <- sum(strata_2023$co2e_mt); peat_2023 <- sum(strata_2023$peat_co2e_mt)
bc_veg_2023 <- sum(bc_2023_strata$co2e_mt); bc_peat_2023 <- sum(bc_2023_strata$peat_co2e_mt)
cause_year <- dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::mutate(strata, region = "Canada"), dplyr::mutate(dplyr::filter(strata, bc), region = "British Columbia")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mha = sum(ha) / 1e6, .by = c(region, year, cause)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(region = factor(region, c("Canada", "British Columbia")), cause = factor(cause, c("Natural", "Human", "Unknown")))

# Fuel burned on a 2 km grid, the Table 2.4 row of each cell's ecological zone and land cover class, with organic soil from the soil raster
grid <- terra::rast(terra::ext(sf::st_bbox(gez)), resolution = 2000, crs = "EPSG:3978")
zone_r <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(gez), grid, field = "gez_abbrev")
zone_code <- terra::levels(zone_r)[[1]]$gez_abbrev[match(terra::values(zone_r)[, 1], terra::levels(zone_r)[[1]]$ID)]
cover_code <- terra::values(terra::project(land_cover, grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
soil_code <- terra::values(terra::project(soil, grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
category <- dplyr::case_when(is.na(zone_code) ~ NA_character_, cover_code %in% c(1:5, 8, 9) ~ "Forest", cover_code %in% 6:7 ~ "Shrubland",
                             cover_code %in% 10:11 ~ "Grassland", cover_code %in% c(12, 14) ~ "Cropland", cover_code == 16 & zone_code == "P" ~ "Tundra",
                             .default = "Other")
category <- dplyr::if_else(zone_code == "P" & category %in% c("Shrubland", "Grassland"), "Tundra", category)
fuel <- dplyr::case_when(category == "Forest" & zone_code %in% c(boreal_zones, "P") ~ 52.8, category == "Forest" ~ 19.8, category == "Shrubland" ~ 14.3,
                         category == "Grassland" ~ 4.1, category == "Tundra" ~ 10, .default = NA_real_)
as_layer <- function(x, levels) { r <- terra::rast(grid); terra::values(r) <- factor(x, levels = levels); r }
# The rows of Table 1 that overlap on each cell, the vegetation row of Table 2.4 and the organic soil row of the Wetlands Supplement, for their areas
row_labels <- c("Boreal forest, mineral soil", "Boreal forest, organic soil", "Temperate forest, mineral soil", "Temperate forest, organic soil",
                "Shrubland", "Grassland", "Tundra")
row_class <- dplyr::case_when(is.na(fuel) ~ NA_character_, fuel == 52.8 & soil_code == 1 ~ row_labels[2], fuel == 52.8 ~ row_labels[1],
                              fuel == 19.8 & soil_code == 1 ~ row_labels[4], fuel == 19.8 ~ row_labels[3], fuel == 14.3 ~ row_labels[5],
                              fuel == 4.1 ~ row_labels[6], fuel == 10 ~ row_labels[7])
row_area <- tibble::tibble(row_class) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(row_class)) |> dplyr::count(row_class) |> dplyr::mutate(mha = n * 400 / 1e6)
soil_r <- as_layer(dplyr::if_else(is.na(zone_code) | soil_code == 0, NA_character_, soil_labels[pmax(soil_code, 1)]), soil_labels)
fuel_area <- tibble::tibble(category, fuel, zone_code) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(zone_code)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mha = dplyr::n() * 400 / 1e6, .by = c(category, fuel)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(-mha)
organic_mha <- sum(!is.na(fuel) & soil_code == 1, na.rm = TRUE) * 400 / 1e6
```

```{r}
fetch("http://ftp.maps.canada.ca/pub/nrcan_rncan/Forestry-industry_Industrie-forestiere/peatlands/ClassPeatMap_2020_EPSG_3978.tif", "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/ClassPeatMap_2020_EPSG_3978.tif")
fetch("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx")

inside <- !is.na(zone_code)
# Codes of the 2026 fuel type raster as its map service labels them, grouped to the fuel of the FBP System
fbp_code <- terra::values(terra::project(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/FBP_FuelTypes_Canada_2026_250m.tiff"), grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
fbp_labels <- c("Conifer, C-1 to C-7", "Mixedwood, M-1 and M-2", "Deciduous, D-1 and D-2", "Grass, O-1", "Vegetated non-fuel", "Non-fuel")
fbp_group <- dplyr::case_when(!inside ~ NA_character_, fbp_code %in% 1:7 ~ fbp_labels[1], fbp_code %in% c(415, 625, 650, 675) ~ fbp_labels[2],
                              fbp_code %in% c(11, 13) ~ fbp_labels[3], fbp_code %in% c(31, 32) ~ fbp_labels[4], fbp_code == 105 ~ fbp_labels[5],
                              fbp_code == 101 ~ fbp_labels[6], .default = NA_character_)
fbp_r <- as_layer(fbp_group, fbp_labels)
fbp_area <- tibble::tibble(fbp_group) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(fbp_group)) |> dplyr::count(fbp_group) |> dplyr::mutate(mha = n * 400 / 1e6) |> dplyr::arrange(-mha)

# Classes 1 to 9 of the peatland map are bog and fen, open, treed and forested; 0 is not peat
peat_code <- terra::values(terra::project(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/ClassPeatMap_2020_EPSG_3978.tif"), grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
peat_labels <- c("Open bog and fen", "Treed bog and fen", "Forested bog and fen")
peat_group <- dplyr::case_when(!inside ~ NA_character_, peat_code %in% 1:3 ~ peat_labels[1], peat_code %in% 4:6 ~ peat_labels[2],
                               peat_code %in% 7:9 ~ peat_labels[3], .default = NA_character_)
cfs_peat_r <- as_layer(peat_group, peat_labels)
mha_of <- function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE) * 400 / 1e6
ipcc_organic_mha <- mha_of(inside & soil_code == 1); cfs_peat_mha <- mha_of(inside & peat_code %in% 1:9)
both_peat_mha <- mha_of(inside & soil_code == 1 & peat_code %in% 1:9)

nbac <- readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", sheet = "sumstats_admin_name", skip = 2) |>
  dplyr::transmute(year = as.integer(YEAR), ha = as.numeric(CANADA)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(year))
nbac_2023 <- nbac$ha[nbac$year == 2023]

# The 2023 fires on the national peatland map and in the national fuel types
points_2023 <- sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath("02.inputs/nfdb/raw/NFDB_point_shp.zip"), "/NFDB_point_20260811.shp"),
                           query = 'SELECT YEAR, SIZE_HA FROM "NFDB_point_20260811" WHERE YEAR = 2023', quiet = TRUE) |>
  sf::st_transform(3978)
points_2023$peat <- terra::extract(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/ClassPeatMap_2020_EPSG_3978.tif"), terra::vect(points_2023))[, 2]
points_2023$fbp <- terra::extract(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/FBP_FuelTypes_Canada_2026_250m.tiff"), terra::vect(points_2023))[, 2]
cfs_peat_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$peat %in% 1:9]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)
conifer_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$fbp %in% 1:7]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)
mixed_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$fbp %in% c(415, 625, 650, 675)]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)
deciduous_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$fbp %in% c(11, 13)]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)

fbp_mha <- function(label) fbp_area$mha[fbp_area$fbp_group == label]
tier2_table <- tibble::tribble(~Quantity, ~`Tier 1 global default`, ~`National dataset`,
  "Forest fuel classes on the 2 km grid", sprintf("Two Table 2.4 rows, boreal forest %.0f Mha and temperate forest %.0f Mha", fuel_area$mha[fuel_area$category == "Forest" & fuel_area$fuel == 52.8], fuel_area$mha[fuel_area$category == "Forest" & fuel_area$fuel == 19.8]),
    sprintf("FBP fuel types, conifer %.0f Mha, mixedwood %.0f Mha, deciduous %.0f Mha, grass %.0f Mha", fbp_mha(fbp_labels[1]), fbp_mha(fbp_labels[2]), fbp_mha(fbp_labels[3]), fbp_mha(fbp_labels[4])),
  "Fuel burned (t dry matter per ha)", "Table 2.4, 52.8 ± 48.4 boreal and 19.8 ± 6.3 temperate", "CBM-CFS3 disturbance matrices on the pools of each stand, with a burn severity sub-model from 2026",
  "Organic soil (Mha)", sprintf("IPCC default raster, %.0f", ipcc_organic_mha), sprintf("Peatland map, %.0f, of which %.0f also organic in the default raster", cfs_peat_mha, both_peat_mha),
  "Area burned in 2023 (Mha)", sprintf("MODIS MCD64A1 other forest as FAO published it, %.1f", burn_2023$ha / 1e6), sprintf("National Burned Area Composite, %.1f; fire points, %.1f", nbac_2023 / 1e6, sum(strata_2023$ha) / 1e6),
  "Area burned in 2023 on organic soil (%)", sprintf("IPCC default raster, %.0f", organic_share_2023), sprintf("Peatland map, %.0f", cfs_peat_share_2023),
  "Area burned in 2023 by fuel (%)", sprintf("MCD12Q1 forest %.0f, woody savanna and savanna %.0f", forest_share_2023, savanna_share_2023), sprintf("FBP conifer %.0f, mixedwood %.0f, deciduous %.0f", conifer_share_2023, mixed_share_2023, deciduous_share_2023),
  "Emission factors (g per kg)", "Table 2.5, 1,569 carbon dioxide, 4.7 methane, 0.26 nitrous oxide", "Inventory split of combusted carbon, 90 per cent carbon dioxide, 9 per cent carbon monoxide, 1 per cent methane",
```

```{r}
#| label: faostat-burned
#| output: false

# MODIS/Terra+Aqua Burned Area Monthly L3 Global 500m SIN Grid, MCD64A1 version 6.1, bands BurnDate and Uncertainty, 2001 to 2024, read through Google Earth Engine
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD64A1.061
# MODIS/Terra+Aqua Land Cover Type Yearly L3 Global 500m SIN Grid, MCD12Q1 version 6.1, band LC_Type1 (IGBP classes), 2001 to 2023, read through Google Earth Engine
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD12Q1.061
# FAO Global Administrative Unit Layers 2015, level 0, the country boundary FAO's note names, Earth Engine collection FAO/GAUL/2015/level0
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/FAO_GAUL_2015_level0
# The burned area of FAO's method rebuilt as its note describes it: burned pixels of MCD64A1 with uncertainty below 20 per cent, the IGBP class
# of the yearly MCD12Q1 map (the 2022 map for 2023 and the 2023 map for 2024, the latest FAO had, which the rebuild showed), counted within the GAUL boundary, with every pixel also keyed by the ecological zone group of its Table 2.4 row
# and by whether the IPCC default soil raster calls its soil organic, so that the zone rows and the peat term can be applied to FAO's own burned area
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/mcd64a1-burned-by-stratum.csv")) {
  zone_groups <- gez |>
    dplyr::mutate(group = dplyr::case_when(gez_abbrev %in% boreal_zones ~ 1L, gez_abbrev == "P" ~ 3L, .default = 2L)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(group) |>
    dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop") |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_simplify(dTolerance = 2000) |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_transform(4326)
  geojson <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
  sf::st_write(zone_groups, geojson, quiet = TRUE)
  organic_cells <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(soil == 1, dissolve = TRUE))
  organic_cells <- sf::st_set_crs(sf::st_make_valid(organic_cells[organic_cells[[1]] == 1, 1]), 4326)
  organic_geojson <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
  sf::st_write(organic_cells, organic_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
  py <- reticulate::import_main()
  py$GEOJSON <- geojson
  py$ORGANIC <- organic_geojson
  py$CSV <- "02.inputs/faostat/mcd64a1-burned-by-stratum.csv"
  py$UNC_MAX <- 20L
  py$TILES <- "02.inputs/faostat/raw/mcd64a1-tiles"
  reticulate::py_run_string(r"(
import ee, json, csv, os, time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
ee.Initialize(project='manuscripts-personal')
# The country, the zone groups and the organic soil enter as painted masks on plain rectangles, because a country polygon used as the
# reduction region is clipped against every tile and never returned for Canada, where the same polygon painted as a mask takes seconds
gaul = ee.FeatureCollection('FAO/GAUL/2015/level0').filter(ee.Filter.eq('ADM0_NAME', 'Canada'))
canada_mask = ee.Image().byte().paint(gaul, 1)
zones = ee.FeatureCollection([ee.Feature(ee.Geometry(f['geometry'], 'EPSG:4326', False), {'group': f['properties']['group']}) for f in json.load(open(GEOJSON))['features']])
organic = ee.FeatureCollection([ee.Feature(ee.Geometry(f['geometry'], 'EPSG:4326', False)) for f in json.load(open(ORGANIC))['features']])
base = ee.Image().byte().paint(zones, 'group').unmask(0).multiply(100).add(ee.Image().byte().paint(organic, 1).unmask(0).multiply(1000))
# Counted in the MODIS sinusoidal grid, where every pixel has the same area, so a pixel count times that area is the burned area exactly
modis = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD12Q1').first().select('LC_Type1').projection()
scale = 463.3127165275
pixel_ha = scale * scale / 1e4
def year_key(year):
    lc_year = 2022 if year == 2023 else min(year, 2023)
    monthly = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD64A1').filterDate(f'{year}-01-01', f'{year + 1}-01-01')
    burned = monthly.map(lambda i: i.select('BurnDate').gt(0).And(i.select('Uncertainty').lt(UNC_MAX))).max()
    cover = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD12Q1').filterDate(f'{lc_year}-01-01', f'{lc_year + 1}-01-01').first().select('LC_Type1')
    return cover.add(base).updateMask(burned).updateMask(canada_mask).rename(f'y{year}')
stack = ee.Image.cat([year_key(year) for year in range(2001, 2025)])
# Canada's extent in 96 boxes of 7.5 by 5.4 degrees, each a direct call holding all 24 years, six calls at a time, each box cached as it lands
os.makedirs(TILES, exist_ok=True)
lons = [-141.5 + i * 7.5 for i in range(13)]
lats = [41 + j * 5.4 for j in range(9)]
boxes = [(f'b{i:02d}{j:02d}', ee.Geometry.Rectangle([lons[i], lats[j], lons[i + 1], lats[j + 1]], 'EPSG:4326', False)) for i in range(12) for j in range(8)]
def run_box(name, box, depth=0):
    path = f'{TILES}/{name}.json'
    if os.path.exists(path):
        return name
    try:
        hist = stack.reduceRegion(reducer=ee.Reducer.frequencyHistogram(), geometry=box, crs=modis, scale=scale, maxPixels=1e11).getInfo()
    except Exception as e:
        if depth >= 2 or 'time' not in str(e).lower():
            raise
        c = box.coordinates().getInfo()[0]
        x0, y0 = c[0]; x1, y1 = c[2]; xm, ym = (x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2
        hist = {}
        for k, (p, q, r, s) in enumerate(((x0, y0, xm, ym), (xm, y0, x1, ym), (x0, ym, xm, y1), (xm, ym, x1, y1))):
            run_box(f'{name}_{k}', ee.Geometry.Rectangle([p, q, r, s], 'EPSG:4326', False), depth + 1)
            for band, h in json.load(open(f'{TILES}/{name}_{k}.json')).items():
                for key, n in (h or {}).items():
                    hist.setdefault(band, {})
                    hist[band][key] = hist[band].get(key, 0) + n
    json.dump(hist, open(path, 'w'))
    return name
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool:
    for done in as_completed([pool.submit(run_box, name, box) for name, box in boxes]):
        done.result()
counts = {}
for name, _ in boxes:
    for band, h in json.load(open(f'{TILES}/{name}.json')).items():
        for key, n in (h or {}).items():
            counts[(int(band[1:]), int(float(key)))] = counts.get((int(band[1:]), int(float(key))), 0) + n
with open(CSV, 'w', newline='') as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['year', 'land_cover_year', 'organic', 'zone_group', 'igbp', 'ha'])
    w.writeheader()
    for (year, k), n in sorted(counts.items()):
        w.writerow({'year': year, 'land_cover_year': 2022 if year == 2023 else min(year, 2023), 'organic': k // 1000, 'zone_group': (k // 100) % 10, 'igbp': k % 100, 'ha': n * pixel_ha})
)")
}
mcd <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/mcd64a1-burned-by-stratum.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(2001:2024 %in% mcd$year))

# FAO's items from the IGBP classes, forest as classes 1 to 5, and its fuel as the Table 2.4 rows its recovered coefficients matched
item_of <- function(igbp) dplyr::case_when(igbp %in% 1:5 ~ "Other forest", igbp == 8 ~ "Woody savanna", igbp == 9 ~ "Savanna", igbp == 10 ~ "Grassland",
                                           igbp == 7 ~ "Open shrubland", igbp == 6 ~ "Closed shrubland")
rebuilt <- mcd |>
  dplyr::mutate(item = item_of(igbp)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(item)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fuel = dplyr::case_when(item == "Other forest" & zone_group == 2 ~ table_2_4$fuel[2], item == "Other forest" ~ table_2_4$fuel[1],
                                        item == "Woody savanna" ~ table_2_4$fuel[3], item %in% c("Savanna", "Grassland") ~ table_2_4$fuel[4],
                                        item == "Open shrubland" ~ table_2_4$fuel[5], item == "Closed shrubland" ~ table_2_4$fuel[6])) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), dm = sum(ha * fuel), .by = c(year, item)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(co2_kt = dplyr::if_else(item == "Other forest", dm * table_2_5$co2[1] / 1e6, NA_real_),
                ch4_kt = dm * table_2_5$ch4[1] / 1e6, n2o_kt = dm * table_2_5$n2o[1] / 1e6)
published <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, item %in% unique(rebuilt$item)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(element = dplyr::case_match(element, "Burned Area" ~ "ha", "Biomass burned (dry matter)" ~ "dm", "Emissions (CO2)" ~ "co2_kt",
                                            "Emissions (CH4)" ~ "ch4_kt", "Emissions (N2O)" ~ "n2o_kt")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(element)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(year, item), names_from = element, values_from = value)
check <- dplyr::inner_join(rebuilt, published, by = c("year", "item"), suffix = c("_rebuilt", "_fao"))
# How closely the rerun reproduced the published hectares, by year over the five items and by item and year, and the forest fuel it implies
repro_year <- dplyr::summarise(check, ratio = sum(ha_rebuilt) / sum(ha_fao), .by = year)
repro_item <- dplyr::mutate(dplyr::filter(check, ha_fao > 0), ratio = ha_rebuilt / ha_fao)
repro_within_2 <- 100 * mean(abs(repro_item$ratio - 1) <= 0.02)
forest_2023 <- dplyr::filter(mcd, year == 2023, igbp %in% 1:5)
fao_fuel_2023 <- sum(forest_2023$ha * dplyr::if_else(forest_2023$zone_group == 2, table_2_4$fuel[2], table_2_4$fuel[1])) / sum(forest_2023$ha)

# The guidelines' own Tier 1 on FAO's burned area: every burned pixel at the Table 2.4 row and the Table 2.5 row of its ecological zone group, as the zone
# rebuild applied them to the fire points, and the peat term of Equation 2.8 on the pixels the soil raster calls organic, with the built up, snow, barren,
# water and unclassified pixels left out as FAO's note excludes them
group_rows <- zone_defaults |>
  dplyr::filter(gez_abbrev %in% c("Ba", "TeDc", "P")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(zone_group = c(Ba = 1L, TeDc = 2L, P = 3L)[gez_abbrev]) |>
  dplyr::select(zone_group, row_2_4, mb_cf, co2, ch4, n2o)
tier1_fao_area <- mcd |>
  dplyr::filter(zone_group %in% 1:3, !igbp %in% c(0, 13, 15, 16, 17)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), organic_ha = sum(ha[organic == 1]), .by = c(year, zone_group)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(group_rows, by = "zone_group") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dm_mt = ha * mb_cf / 1e6, co2_mt = dm_mt * co2 / 1e3, ch4_kt = dm_mt * ch4, n2o_kt = dm_mt * n2o,
                co2e_mt = co2_mt + (ch4_kt * 28 + n2o_kt * 265) / 1e3,
                peat_mt = organic_ha * peat_fuel[["mean"]] / 1e6, peat_co2_mt = peat_mt * peat_ef$co2 / 1e3, peat_ch4_kt = peat_mt * peat_ef$ch4,
                peat_co2e_mt = peat_co2_mt + peat_ch4_kt * 28 / 1e3)
rung2_2023 <- dplyr::filter(tier1_fao_area, year == 2023) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), organic_ha = sum(organic_ha), co2_mt = sum(co2_mt), ch4_kt = sum(ch4_kt), n2o_kt = sum(n2o_kt), co2e_mt = sum(co2e_mt),
                   peat_co2_mt = sum(peat_co2_mt), peat_ch4_kt = sum(peat_ch4_kt), peat_co2e_mt = sum(peat_co2e_mt))

# The 2023 estimate rung by rung, each rung replacing one input of the rung above, carbon dioxide equivalent at the inventory's warming potentials
co2e_of <- function(co2_kt, ch4_kt, n2o_kt) (sum(co2_kt, na.rm = TRUE) + 28 * sum(ch4_kt) + 265 * sum(n2o_kt)) / 1e3
fao_2023_items <- dplyr::filter(published, year == 2023)
rebuilt_2023 <- dplyr::filter(rebuilt, year == 2023)
ladder <- tibble::tribble(~Estimate, ~`Burned area`, ~`Fuel and emission factors`, ~ha, ~co2_mt, ~ch4_kt, ~co2e_mt,
  "FAO as published", "MCD64A1 by MCD12Q1 class", "One fuel value per item, savanna factors",
    sum(fao_2023_items$ha), sum(fao_2023_items$co2_kt, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e3, sum(fao_2023_items$ch4_kt), co2e_of(fao_2023_items$co2_kt, fao_2023_items$ch4_kt, fao_2023_items$n2o_kt),
  "FAO rebuilt from its note", "MCD64A1 by MCD12Q1 class", "The same",
    sum(rebuilt_2023$ha), sum(rebuilt_2023$co2_kt, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e3, sum(rebuilt_2023$ch4_kt), co2e_of(rebuilt_2023$co2_kt, rebuilt_2023$ch4_kt, rebuilt_2023$n2o_kt),
  "Tier 1 by zone on FAO's area", "MCD64A1 by ecological zone", "Table 2.4 and 2.5 rows of the zone",
    rung2_2023$ha, rung2_2023$co2_mt, rung2_2023$ch4_kt, rung2_2023$co2e_mt,
  "Tier 1 by zone and soil on FAO's area", "MCD64A1 by zone and soil class", "The same, with the peat term on organic soil",
    rung2_2023$ha, rung2_2023$co2_mt + rung2_2023$peat_co2_mt, rung2_2023$ch4_kt + rung2_2023$peat_ch4_kt, rung2_2023$co2e_mt + rung2_2023$peat_co2e_mt,
  "Tier 1 by zone on the fire points", "Fire points by ecological zone", "The same",
    sum(zone_2023$ha), sum(zone_2023$co2_mt), sum(zone_2023$ch4_kt), sum(zone_2023$co2e_mt),
  "Tier 1 by stratum with the peat term", "Fire points by zone, fire type and soil", "Rows by fire type and the Wetlands Supplement",
    sum(strata_2023$ha), sum(strata_2023$co2_mt + strata_2023$peat_co2_mt), sum(strata_2023$ch4_kt + strata_2023$peat_ch4_kt), veg_2023 + peat_2023)
ladder_table <- dplyr::transmute(ladder, Estimate, `Burned area`, `Fuel and emission factors`, `Burned (Mha)` = sprintf("%.1f", ha / 1e6),
                                 `CO2 (Mt)` = sprintf("%.0f", co2_mt), `CH4 (kt)` = sprintf("%.0f", ch4_kt), `CO2e (Mt)` = sprintf("%.0f", co2e_mt))
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Canada's managed forest showed emission reductions under a crediting standard in most years when its national inventory disaggregated natural from anthropogenic disturbances. That inventory, submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, left emissions and removals of lands affected by wildfire and insects out of its total. No study had measured the effect of the disaggregation on the emission reductions a government could sell. This study applied the ART TREES standard to Canada's 2026 inventory for the crediting years 2017 to 2024 and rebuilt the Food and Agriculture Organization's Tier 1 fire emissions. The disaggregated and undisaggregated accounts were compared with a threshold account excluding natural disturbances only in fire years above a 13 year baseline. The disaggregated account showed emission reductions in `r sum(split_pos)` of `r nrow(credits)` years, `r round(sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]), 1)` million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. Those reductions carried uncertainty adjustment factors of `r format(min(uncertainty[["Disaggregated deduction (%)"]], na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")` to `r format(max(uncertainty[["Disaggregated deduction (%)"]], na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")` per cent, from the Monte Carlo 90 per cent confidence interval. The undisaggregated account exceeded the crediting level by `r format(abs(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][worst]), big.mark = ",")` million tonnes in `r credits$Year[worst]` alone, a reversal larger than the buffer. The threshold account gave `r round(sum(credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]][rule_pos]), 1)` million tonnes, `r round(sum(credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]][rule_pos]) / sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]), 1)` times the disaggregated account, because ordinary fire years raised the threshold account's crediting level. The Tier 1 burned area was reproduced within `r round(100 * max(abs(repro_year$ratio - 1)))` per cent, and the Tier 1 emission factors were recovered. A standard accepting the disaggregation needed a record length and regrowth period, exclusion only of emissions above a background level and uncertainty deducted from gross emissions and removals.

# Introduction

National greenhouse gas inventories reported the land sector on the assumption that every emission and removal on managed land was caused by people [@kurz2018quantifying]. Managed land thereby stood in for human activity, and the 2019 Refinement to the IPCC Guidelines called this assumption the managed land proxy, abbreviated there as MLP. In Canada's managed forest the assumption added the emissions and later removals of fire and insects to those of harvest and regrowth. The effect of management was thereby hidden in the reported trend [@kurz2018quantifying]. The Refinement took Canada's series for 1990 to 2016 as its example and offered "an approach that countries can apply on a voluntary basis within the MLP in order to indicate those emissions and removals considered to result from human activity, and those that are understood to result from natural disturbances" [@ogle2019generic]. The approach assumed that the carbon dioxide released would "be balanced by subsequent removals across the landscape at some future point in time" [@ogle2019generic]. In July 2024 an IPCC expert meeting in Ispra recorded that natural disturbance emissions "may be disaggregated from the total, but the total must be reported" [@ipcc2024reconciling].

The rule that every disturbance on managed land was reported began in 2003. The Good Practice Guidance held that omitting natural disturbance losses "would overestimate carbon uptakes" [@ipcc2003gpg, p. 1.11]. It asked for all disturbed areas in managed forest "irrespective of whether these were the result of human activity" [@ipcc2003gpg, p. 3.27]. Factoring out was "currently under consideration by the IPCC and will therefore not be addressed further here" [@ipcc2003gpg, p. 4.33]. The IPCC wrote accounting rules for natural disturbance once, for the second Kyoto commitment period. The 2013 Supplement replaced the test of cause with "beyond the control of, and not materially influenced by a Party", because a wildfire's "immediate cause may be difficult to determine" [@ipcc2014kp, p. 2.36]. It excluded only the emissions above a background level built from a calibration period, and every later removal on the same land [@ipcc2014kp, pp. 2.46 to 2.53]. The 2019 Refinement carried the definition into reporting guidance word for word and carried none of the rules [@ogle2019generic, p. 2.69].

The effect of the assumption in Canada was known before the Refinement. CBM-CFS3, the Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector, was run with future fire and insect outbreaks drawn at random. It projected the managed forest as a net source of 30 to 245 Mt CO~2~e a year over 2008 to 2012. Canada therefore did not count forest management under the Kyoto Protocol [@kurz2008risk]. Canada's 2017 inventory then divided the managed forest into land dominated by natural disturbance and the rest, two parts that summed to the net emissions of the whole [@kurz2018quantifying]. A burned stand stayed in the natural disturbance part until it had enough wood to be worth cutting. That took 60 years nationally in 2017 and later 60 to 100 years by region [@kurz2018quantifying; @kurz2024revised]. A revised harvest record for 1889 to 1989 moved 34 million hectares into that part. It cut the human sink reported for 1990 by 113 Mt CO~2~e, or 56 per cent, without any change in the forest [@kurz2024revised]. The model's fire matrices assumed that every fire burned at high severity. A sub-model built on mapped burn severity gave regional emissions typically 10 to 25 per cent lower [@thompson2026incorporating].

Australia's inventory classed a whole fire season as natural when national fire emissions exceeded the mean of a 2000 to 2012 baseline by two standard deviations. A state's burned area then had to exceed its own mean by one standard deviation [@bowman2023wildfire]. The 2023 fire season in Canada burned `r sprintf("%.1f", nbac_2023 / 1e6)` Mha on the National Burned Area Composite [@cfs2026nbac]. Inverse modelling of satellite carbon monoxide put its emissions at 647 Tg of carbon, with a range of 570 to 727, "comparable to the annual fossil fuel emissions of large nations" [@byrne2024carbon]. Whether such a year counted as natural depended on the record it was tested against.

A percentage uncertainty was the interval divided by the reported value, so a balance near zero had an uncertainty larger than itself whatever method produced the interval. The 2019 uncertainty chapter advised caution "in cases where the point estimate is very small when compared with the size of the confidence interval" [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. The interval of Canada's own model was 32.2 Tg C a year wide, which @metsaranta2017uncertainty stated "cannot be meaningfully expressed in percentage terms because its range of possible values contains zero".

FAOSTAT, the statistical database of the Food and Agriculture Organization, gave every government an independent estimate of its fire emissions. The IPCC recommended it for checking an inventory's activity data, the measured quantities such as burned area, and its emission estimates. Its five page methodological note gave the equation and the layers, but not the row of Table 2.4 each zone took [@fao2025fires]. FAO set the emissions of fires in organic soils to zero outside Southeast Asia, publishing the full values in a separate table [@fao2025fires].

What the disaggregation was worth was set by the crediting standard, the rules under which the reported reductions of a country or province became credits. The standard here was that of the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions, The REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard, cited as ART TREES, which stated that "only anthropogenic emissions shall be considered, and IPCC guidance shall be adhered to on any exclusion of non-anthropogenic emissions" [@art2021trees]. Its 2025 draft added that natural disturbances "may be excluded if they are 'non-anthropogenic events or non-anthropogenic circumstances that cause significant emissions and are beyond the control of, and not materially influenced by a country'" [@art2025trees3; @ogle2019generic]. The Methods set out its uncertainty deduction, buffer and reversal rule.

No study found had run the account of a country or province through a crediting standard both with and without the disaggregation. The nearest compared Canada's reported series under different divisions of the managed forest [@kurz2024revised; @bysouth2024high] or mapped reversal risk without reference to an inventory [@wu2026global]. This study therefore tested the natural disturbance approach of the 2019 Refinement on Canada and British Columbia over 1990 to 2024, the period of the 2026 national inventory. The objective was to compare what each reported, and what each could have been credited under ART TREES, with and without the approach. A third account followed a threshold rule. Because the Refinement set no length for the record behind a natural disturbance test, baselines of 13, 20 and 30 years were compared. The fire emissions FAOSTAT published for Canada were then rebuilt from its stated method, by ecological zone and by stratum. The rebuilt estimate was set beside the national datasets that a higher tier would use.

# Materials and Methods

## Data sources

Thirteen datasets were read. Canada's inventory came as Table 6-1 of the 2026 National Inventory Report, 1990 to 2024, from Environment and Climate Change Canada. Its fire polygons and fire points came from the Canadian National Fire Database of Natural Resources Canada, 1990 to 2024. FAOSTAT supplied its Emissions from Fires domain, 1990 to 2024, and the AllFires_OrganicSoils table FAO released beside it, 1990 to 2021. The two MODIS products behind that domain were read in Google Earth Engine, MCD64A1 burned area for 2001 to 2024 [@giglio2021mcd64a1] and MCD12Q1 land cover for 2001 to 2023 [@friedl2022mcd12q1]. Both were summed within the GAUL 2015 boundary of Canada that FAO's note named. The ecological zones came from FAO's 2010 map, the default stratification of the 2006 Guidelines [@fao2012gez]. The soil classes came from the 5 arc minute IPCC default raster derived from the Harmonized World Soil Database [@batjes2010ipcc]. The fire points carried each fire's cause, type and month [@cfs2026nfdb]. Three national layers were read beside them, the fuel types of the Fire Behaviour Prediction System [@cfs2026fbp], the peatland map of the Canadian Forest Service [@webster2018spatially] and the burned area totals of the National Burned Area Composite [@cfs2026nbac].

## Disaggregation guidance

The disaggregation followed section 2.6 of Volume 4, Chapter 2 of the 2019 Refinement [@ogle2019generic]. That section stated that voluntary disaggregation "may provide a clearer picture of the impact of management activities" [@ogle2019generic]. Section 2.6.3 set out four elements. The total was estimated under the proxy, and the country described how it applied the definition of natural disturbance. The emissions and later removals due to natural disturbance were identified at the stand or the landscape level, and that part was subtracted from the total [@ogle2019generic]. It was "good practice that subsequent removals are also disaggregated until the balance has been reached" [@ogle2019generic]. Its examples were Australia, Canada and a member state of the European Union, in Boxes 2.2i to 2.2k [@ogle2019generic]. The 2013 Supplement had set one, a calibration period that contained "but are not limited to, 1990–2009" [@ipcc2014kp, p. 2.46]. Its default method took the mean and standard deviation of the annual natural disturbance emissions by Equation 2.3.1. Any year above the mean plus twice the standard deviation was removed and both statistics recomputed until no outlier remained. The final mean was the background level and twice the final standard deviation the margin [@ipcc2014kp]. Emissions were excluded "only when the annual emissions are greater than the background level plus the margin", and then only "those emissions that are greater than the background level" [@ipcc2014kp, p. 2.50].

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 2.3.1** [Calculation of the standard deviation for the annual emissions for the calibration period]{.smallcaps}

$$SD = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(x_{i} - \bar{X}\right)^{2} \Big/ \left(N - 1\right)}$$

Where\
$x_{i}$ = the emission estimate for year $i$, $i$ = 1, 2…, $N$ where $N$ is the number of years in the calibration period for which emission estimates are available.\
$\bar{X}$ = the arithmetic mean of all $x_{i}$, i.e. $\bar{X} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} x_{i} / N$.

Reproduced from Chapter 2 of the 2013 Revised Supplementary Methods and Good Practice Guidance Arising from the Kyoto Protocol, page 2.49 [@ipcc2014kp].
:::

## Accounts and crediting

Canada reported its land use sector in Table 6-1 of the 2026 national inventory report, seven categories and their total [@eccc2026nir]. Beneath the total it gave one more line, natural disturbances, marked "Not a reporting category" and "provided solely for transparency purposes" [@eccc2026nir]. That line held the net balance of emissions and removals from natural disturbances in the managed forest, and the total above it left that balance out (Online Resource 1). Every wildfire in the managed forest went to that line, whatever its cause, and stayed there with its regrowth until the stand had enough wood to be worth cutting. Fires that killed a fifth or less of a mature stand, slash burning and prescribed burning stayed in the total [@eccc2026nir]. Two series were read from the table for Canada and for British Columbia, the reported total, the disaggregated account, and that total plus the natural disturbance line, the undisaggregated account. Both came from Canada's National Forest Carbon Monitoring, Accounting and Reporting System. Its core model, CBM-CFS3, grew each stand along a yield curve and moved its carbon through a disturbance matrix [@kurz2018quantifying]. The two accounts were compared over 1990 to 2024 by the mean and standard deviation of their annual net emissions, following @kurz2024revised.

```{r}
#| label: fig-inventory
```

A third account, the threshold account, left the natural disturbance line out only in a year a threshold test classed as natural, the form of test Australia's inventory applied [@bowman2023wildfire]. The threshold rule was run on FAOSTAT's forest fire carbon dioxide series for Canada, 2001 to 2024. A year counted as natural when its emissions exceeded the baseline mean by two standard deviations, on baselines of 13, 20 and 30 years. The 13 year baseline then built the threshold account from the two inventory lines, leaving the natural disturbance line out in a natural year and keeping it in every other. Canada published that line once a year with the regrowth of earlier disturbances inside it, so the threshold account left out that regrowth in a natural year. Australia's inventory instead tracked the land of an excluded fire "until the time forest carbon has returned to its original state" [@bowman2023wildfire]. For British Columbia the rule's second step was applied, under which a season counted as natural in a state only if "the area burned in each state and territory exceeds by one standard deviation the average area burned during the 2000–2012 baseline" [@bowman2023wildfire]. The province's burned area was taken from the fire database over 2001 to 2013.

The crediting level was the mean emissions of the five year reference period, 2012 to 2016, Equation 1 of ART TREES. The reduction in each crediting year, 2017 to 2024, was that level minus the year's emissions, its Equation 12 [@art2021trees]. Both were computed on the three accounts. The uncertainty deduction followed Equations 10 and 11, reproduced below. The buffer withheld 25 per cent of the same quantity, or 5 per cent where three mitigating factors were met. Five percentage points were added for five years after a reversal [@art2021trees].

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 10** [Uncertainty Deduction]{.smallcaps}

$$UNC_{t} = \left(GHG\ ER_{t} + GHG\ RMV_{t}\right) \times UA_{t}$$

**EQUATION 11** [Uncertainty Adjustment Factor]{.smallcaps}

$$UA_{t} = 0.524417 \times \frac{90\%\ CI_{t}}{1.645006}$$

Where\
$UNC_{t}$ = TREES uncertainty deduction in year t; tCO2e\
$UA_{t}$ = TREES uncertainty adjustment factor in year t\
$GHG\ ER_{t}$, $GHG\ RMV_{t}$ = GHG emission reductions and removals in year t; tCO2e\
0.524417 = t value at ART allowable risk\
$90\%\ CI_{t}$ = Half width of 90% confidence interval as a percent of the mean; %\
1.645006 = t value at 90% confidence level

Reproduced from ART TREES version 2.0, pages 46 to 47 [@art2021trees].
:::

The uncertainty of each account followed Approach 2 of the Refinement's uncertainty chapter, Monte Carlo simulation [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. The published uncertainty of CBM-CFS3 was a 95 per cent interval 32.2 Tg C a year wide, 16.6 above its median and 15.6 below [@metsaranta2017uncertainty]. The larger side over 1.96 gave a standard deviation that was applied to every annual value of every account. That assumed the model was no more certain of a megafire year than of a quiet one. Each run drew the five reference years and the crediting year from normal distributions with that standard deviation, and ten thousand runs gave the distribution of each year's reduction. Half the distance between its 5th and 95th percentiles over its mean was the 90 per cent confidence interval of Equation 11. Those draws treated the error of each year as independent, where ART TREES excluded model error as "consistent between emissions in the crediting level and crediting periods" [@art2021trees]. The share of error variance common to all years was therefore varied. Under the normal model it left the mean unchanged and scaled the half width by the square root of the unshared share. The share at which every positive year kept a credit was solved from the same relation. The period deduction the standard allowed "based on the summed uncertainty of gross emission reductions and removals during the total period" was simulated with the same draws for the disaggregated and the threshold account [@art2021trees].

## Fire emission method

Fire emissions in every tier followed Equation 2.27 of Volume 4, Chapter 2 of the 2006 Guidelines, one formula with the tiers differing in the data behind it [@aalde2006generic]. The decision tree of its Figure 2.6 sent a country to Tier 3 where "detailed data on biomass burning" could feed "advanced models or methods", to Tier 2 where "country-specific activity data emission factors" existed, and otherwise to "aggregate data and default emission factors" [@aalde2006generic]. FAO's Statistics Division applied the last in Google Earth Engine and published the sums in FAOSTAT for forest fires, savanna fires and fires in organic soils [@fao2025fires]. Its note gave the burned pixels of MCD64A1 with uncertainty below 20 per cent and the IGBP class of the yearly MCD12Q1 map. Forest was classes 1 to 5, the savanna items classes 6 to 10, and the fuel came from Table 2.4 by ecological zone. That method was rerun in Earth Engine for 2001 to 2024, with the forest fuel of each pixel set by its zone. Each item's burned area, biomass and gases were compared with the values FAO published. The coefficients FAO used were recovered from its published values for Canada, biomass burned over burned area and each gas over biomass burned. They were compared with Tables 2.4 and 2.5 [@aalde2006generic; @fao2025fires]. Each year's value was also compared with the value Canada submitted for the same item.

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 2.27** [Estimation of greenhouse gas emissions from fire]{.smallcaps}

$$L_{\text{fire}} = A \cdot M_{B} \cdot C_{f} \cdot G_{ef} \cdot 10^{-3}$$

Where\
$L_{\text{fire}}$ = amount of greenhouse gas emissions from fire, tonnes of each GHG e.g., CH~4~, N~2~O, etc.\
$A$ = area burnt, ha\
$M_{B}$ = mass of fuel available for combustion, tonnes ha^-1^\
$C_{f}$ = combustion factor, dimensionless\
$G_{ef}$ = emission factor, g kg^-1^ dry matter burnt

Reproduced from Chapter 2 of Volume 4 of the 2006 Guidelines, pages 2.42 to 2.43, with the notes under the terms omitted [@aalde2006generic].
:::

Where data for M~B~ and C~f~ were not available, Tier 1 took a default for their product from Table 2.4 [@aalde2006generic]. The 2019 Refinement reissued the table with the same boreal and temperate rows [@ogle2019generic]. The uncertainty of the Tier 1 estimate was propagated by Equations 3.1 and 3.2 of the uncertainty chapter [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. Each term's uncertainty was 1.96 times the printed standard error or standard deviation over its mean. The chapter called the rule "reasonably accurate as long as the percentage uncertainty is less than approximately 30%" [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. The fuel took the boreal and other temperate rows of Table 2.4, and the emission factor the savanna and grassland row of Table 2.5 that FAO used. Burned area carried no error.

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 3.1 (UPDATED)** [Combining uncertainties, Approach 1, multiplication]{.smallcaps}

$$U_{\text{total}} = \sqrt{U_{1}^{2} + \ldots + U_{i}^{2} + \ldots + U_{n}^{2}}$$

**EQUATION 3.2 (UPDATED)** [Combining uncertainties, Approach 1, addition and subtraction]{.smallcaps}

$$U_{\text{total}} = \frac{\sqrt{\left(U_{1} \cdot x_{1}\right)^{2} + \ldots + \left(U_{i} \cdot x_{i}\right)^{2} + \ldots + \left(U_{n} \cdot x_{n}\right)^{2}}}{\left| x_{1} + \ldots + x_{i} + \ldots + x_{n} \right|}$$

Where\
$U_{\text{total}}$ = the percentage uncertainty of the product or sum, half the 95 percent confidence interval over the total\
$U_{i}$ = the percentage uncertainty of each quantity\
$x_{i}$ = the quantities combined

Reproduced from Chapter 3 of Volume 1 of the 2019 Refinement, pages 3.18 to 3.19 [@paciornik2019uncertainties].
:::

## Strata

The defaults were stratified by vegetation. The guidelines took as their default the ecological zones of the Food and Agriculture Organization, listed in Table 4.1 of the forest land chapter [@aalde2006generic]. Canada fell in `r xfun::numbers_to_words(nrow(gez))` ecological zones on land, `r sprintf("%.0f", sum(gez$mha[gez$gez_abbrev %in% c("Ba", "Bb", "BM")]))` Mha of them boreal, and each took the row of Tables 2.4, 2.5 and 2.6 that its vegetation matched (@fig-zones, Online Resource 2). Three more layers stratified the fire record. The soil raster gave eight classes, organic, sandy, wetland, volcanic, spodic, high activity clay, low activity clay and other [@batjes2010ipcc]. The MCD12Q1 map of 2023 kept its IGBP classes as FAO grouped them, forest for classes 1 to 5 and savanna and grassland for 6 to 10 [@fao2025fires]. The fire record supplied each fire's cause, natural, human or unknown, its type, crown, surface or ground where an agency had recorded it, and its month [@cfs2026nfdb].

```{r}
fmt_tbl(defaults, right = c("Area (Mha)", "Fuel burned (t/ha)", "Combustion factor", "CO2 (g/kg)", "CH4 (g/kg)", "N2O (g/kg)"))
```

Map lines delineate study areas and do not necessarily depict accepted national boundaries."

```{r}
outline_layer <- ggplot2::geom_sf(data = canada_outline, fill = NA, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.15)

p_b <- ggplot2::ggplot() + tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = fbp_r, maxcell = 3e5) + outline_layer +

```

Each fire was placed in the zone, soil class and land cover class at its reported location, and in British Columbia where that fell inside the province. Its fuel burned per hectare was the Table 2.4 row of its zone and fire type (@tbl-rows). Boreal crown and surface fires took their own rows and other boreal fires the general wildfire row. Temperate fires took the wildfire row of other temperate forests and polar fires the tundra row. Grassland fires of April to June took the early dry season row and later fires the mid or late season row. Table 2.4 gave peat a fuel of 41 ± 1.4 tonnes per hectare and no emission factor [@aalde2006generic]. The 2013 Wetlands Supplement supplied both in Equation 2.8 and its Tables 2.6 and 2.7, for fires on undrained as well as drained organic soils [@ipcc2014wetlands, p. 2.39]. A fire on organic soil therefore carried a second term, the undrained peat row of 66 tonnes per hectare with the boreal and temperate emission factors.

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 2.8** [Annual CO~2~-C and non-CO~2~ emissions from organic soil fire]{.smallcaps}

$$L_{\text{fire}} = A \cdot M_{B} \cdot C_{f} \cdot G_{ef} \cdot 10^{-3}$$

Where\
$L_{\text{fire}}$ = amount of CO~2~ or non-CO~2~ emissions, e.g. CH~4~ from fire, tonnes\
$A$ = total area burnt annually, ha\
$M_{B}$ = mass of fuel available for combustion, tonnes ha^-1^ (i.e. mass of dry organic soil fuel)\
$C_{f}$ = combustion factor, dimensionless\
$G_{ef}$ = emission factor for each gas, g kg^-1^ dry matter burnt

Reproduced from Chapter 2 of the 2013 Wetlands Supplement, page 2.39, with the references to its tables omitted [@ipcc2014wetlands].
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rows
#| tbl-cap: "Rows of Tables 2.4 and 2.6 of the 2006 Guidelines for Canada's vegetation, fuel burned as mean and standard error, combustion factor as mean and standard deviation, and the Table 2.5 row of their emission factors, with the organic soil rows of the 2013 Wetlands Supplement, mean and 95 per cent interval, whose Table 2.7 gave 362 ± 41 g of carbon dioxide carbon and 9 ± 4 g of methane per kilogram. A blank is a value the table did not print."

readr::write_csv(rows_table, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-rows.csv")
fmt_tbl(rows_table, right = c("Fuel burned (t/ha)", "Combustion factor"))
```

The estimate was rebuilt by zone, every fire of 2001 to 2024 summed by zone and year and multiplied by the fuel burned and emission factors of its row. Methane and nitrous oxide were converted at the inventory's warming potentials of 28 and 265 [@eccc2026nir]. Zones sharing a row shared its error, so their emissions were summed before the rows were combined in quadrature. It was rebuilt again by stratum for Canada and British Columbia, each fire at the row of its zone and type, with the peat term on organic soil. The area burned was summed by year and cause. The zone rows were also applied to FAO's own burned area, each MCD64A1 pixel at the rows of its zone group. The 2023 estimate thus changed one input at a time, from FAO's method to the strata with the peat term. The rows were also laid on a 2 km grid from the zone and land cover of each cell, with the organic soil row where the soil raster was organic. On that grid forest took in woody savanna and savanna, classes 8 and 9, whose tree cover exceeded 10 per cent. Each default had a national counterpart at a higher tier, so three national layers were set beside the defaults term by term (@fig-zones). The fuel types of the Fire Behaviour Prediction System, 2026 release, were grouped into conifer, mixedwood, deciduous, grass and non-fuel from the labels of the catalogue's map service [@cfs2026fbp]. The peatland map of the Canadian Forest Service gave bog and fen by canopy at 250 m [@webster2018spatially]. The National Burned Area Composite, the inventory's source of burned area, gave the national total for each year [@cfs2026nbac; @eccc2026nir]. Each layer was projected to the 2 km grid, and the 2023 fires were placed on the peatland map and the fuel types. The organic soil of the IPCC raster was compared cell by cell with the peatland map.

# Results

## Crediting

Disaggregating natural disturbance cut the standard deviation of Canada's annual land use emissions from `r round(stats::sd(national$net))` to `r round(stats::sd(national$human))` Mt CO~2~e over 1990 to 2024, a factor of `r round(stats::sd(national$net) / stats::sd(national$human), 1)` (Online Resource 6). The account Canada reported averaged `r msd(national$human)`. Without the disaggregation the same land averaged `r msd(national$net)`. In 2023 Canada reported `r national$human[national$year == 2023]` Mt where the undisaggregated account showed `r format(round(national$net[national$year == 2023]), big.mark = ",")` Mt. British Columbia's reported account averaged `r msd(province$human)`. Without the disaggregation it averaged `r msd(province$net)`, a standard deviation `r round(stats::sd(province$net) / stats::sd(province$human), 1)` times larger. In 2023 the province reported `r province$human[province$year == 2023]` Mt against `r round(province$net[province$year == 2023])` Mt. The baseline length moved the threshold but not the classification. Lengthening it from 13 to 20 years raised the threshold `r round(100 * (baselines[["Threshold (kt)"]][2] / baselines[["Threshold (kt)"]][1] - 1))` per cent and classed the same `r length(strsplit(baselines[["Years classified natural"]][1], ", ")[[1]])` years as natural, `r sub(", ([0-9]+)$", " and \\1", baselines[["Years classified natural"]][1])`. A 30 year baseline could not be run on a series of `r nrow(forest_co2)` years.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-credits
#| tbl-cap: "Net emissions, crediting level and emission reduction for Canada's managed land under three accounts, 2017 to 2024. The crediting level is the mean of 2012 to 2016, Equation 1 of ART TREES, and the reduction is the level minus the year's net emissions, Equation 12. The threshold account leaves out the natural disturbance line only in years the 13 year baseline classes as natural. A negative reduction is a reversal."

readr::write_csv(credits_table, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-credits.csv")
fmt_tbl(credits_table)
```

On the account Canada reported, reductions were positive in `r sum(split_pos)` of the `r nrow(credits)` crediting years and summed to `r round(sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]), 1)` Mt of carbon dioxide equivalent. Without the disaggregation, reductions were positive in only `r sum(whole_pos)` years. The shortfall in `r credits$Year[worst]` alone reached `r format(abs(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][worst]), big.mark = ",")` Mt, `r round(abs(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][worst]) / sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]))` times every reduction the disaggregated account achieved over the period (@tbl-credits). An undisaggregated account of this land therefore exhausted its buffer in `r credits$Year[which(!whole_pos)[1]]` and in each later year above the level. The reversal rule retired buffer credits equal to the lower of the excess or every credit issued [@art2021trees]. The threshold account gave more credit than either. It left out the natural disturbance line in `r paste(natural_years[natural_years <= 2016], collapse = " and ")`, the only reference year the rule classed as natural. That set the crediting level at `r round(level_rule, 1)` Mt against `r round(level_split, 1)` Mt on the disaggregated and `r round(level_whole, 1)` Mt on the undisaggregated account. Reductions were positive in `r sum(rule_pos)` of the `r nrow(credits)` years and summed to `r round(sum(credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]][rule_pos]), 1)` Mt, `r round(sum(credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]][rule_pos]) / sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]), 1)` times the disaggregated total (@tbl-credits). British Columbia, with `r bc_credits[["Burned area share (%)"]][bc_credits$Year == 2023]` per cent of the area burned in Canada in 2023, followed the same pattern more sharply (Online Resource 3). Its disaggregated reductions were positive in `r sum(bc_split_pos)` of `r nrow(bc_credits)` years and summed to `r round(sum(bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][bc_split_pos]), 1)` Mt, where the undisaggregated account fell `r format(abs(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][bc_worst]), big.mark = ",")` Mt below the crediting level in `r bc_credits$Year[bc_worst]`. Under the threshold rule its largest shortfall fell in `r bc_credits$Year[bc_rule_worst]`, a year the national test classed as ordinary although the province burned `r format(round(bc_ha(bc_credits$Year[bc_rule_worst])), big.mark = ",")` hectares, `r round(bc_ha(bc_credits$Year[bc_rule_worst]) / bc_threshold_ha, 1)` times its own threshold.
